 League of Legends World Champion Cyanide Dies at 31
 League of Legends 
 Sonu Banerjee 
 26 Oct 2026, 5:19 PM IST 
 1 min. read 
 Facebook X WhatsApp Telegram Copy URL 
 Add as preferred source 
 Lauri “Cyanide” Happonen, the Finnish League of Legends prodigy who helped Fnatic win the first League of Legends World Championship, has reportedly passed away at the age of 31.
 The news was first brought to light by Finnish outlet Ilta-Sanomat . As per the report, he died on July 31, 2026, but the exact cause of his death has not been made public.
 Lauri ”Cyanide” Happonen has past away at the age of 31 
 by u/taalaporriainen in leagueoflegends 
 For the unaware, Cyanide was one of the youngest stars in the early years of LoL. During his tenure with Fnatic, he became the youngest player ever to win Worlds at just 16 years of age. The 2011 title was also a huge milestone for the region, as it was the first World Championship won by a European team, and it remains the only one taken by a team from outside Asia.
 - Advertisement - 
 He stayed with Fnatic through 2014. He then proceeded to play for Origen from 2015 to 2017 alongside his close friend xPeke. He was still involved in the community this year, participating in the League Classic showmatch on July 24 as part of Team Dynasty.
 Shortly after the news surfaced on the internet, Fnatic expressed its condolences via an X post .

 “We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Lauri ‘Cyanide’ Happonen earlier this year,” the org said. “During his four-year spell at Fnatic, Cyanide made history as the youngest ever player to win Worlds at just 16. He leaves behind a legacy that will never be forgotten.”
 We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Lauri “Cyanide" Happonen earlier this year.
During his four-year spell at Fnatic, Cyanide made history as the youngest ever player to win Worlds at just 16. He leaves behind a legacy that will never be forgotten.
Our heartfelt… pic.twitter.com/c2CzyqInSo 
— FNATIC (@FNATIC) October 26, 2026 
 Former teammate YellOwStaR also paid tribute to the legend, saying Cyanide was “much more than a teammate” to him.
 “He was one of the kindest, most genuine souls I’ve ever had the privilege of knowing,” he said. “We saw each other again at the showmatch in July, and he was still full of dreams, plans, and projects for the future. You will be deeply missed, brother. Thank you for the memories, the time we shared, and for the person you were”
 This photo will forever be our last memory together.. @OGCyanide 
💔
Lauri was so much more than a teammate. We shared our everyday lives for over two and a half years, and he became so much more than just someone I played alongside.
He was one of the kindest, most genuine souls… pic.twitter.com/WbxMmYJOOG 
— YellOwStaR (@YellOwStaRL0L) October 26, 2026 
 It’s safe to say that Cyanide will forever be remembered as a pioneer of competitive League of Legends and as a player who helped put European esports on the map.
